channel.title: The Dig — Application benchmarks
channel.description: Papers relevant to operating, benchmarking, integrating and using a semiconductor spin-qubit quantum computer of at least 16 qubits that is co-located with and integrated into an HPC system. Today's arXiv announcement, ranked against the Application benchmarks preset. Today’s ranked reading list puts two relevance-4 papers first: 2611.27140, on FPGA-in-loop drift tracking and charge-jump recovery for autonomously retuning spin-qubit operating points, and 2611.27927, on calibration-aware, transpilation-predicted multi-vendor QPU scheduling that could transfer to an HPC queue managing a small noisy spin-qubit device. The two relevance-3 skims follow: 2611.27896 offers an eighth-order Trotter-Suzuki circuit-synthesis plugin and gate-depth comparisons, while 2611.26884 proposes Trotter-step ordering to reduce circuit depth and Trotter error; both are indirectly useful for the software and application-benchmark stack but lack spin-qubit, calibration, or HPC-integration results.
